title: Discographical puzzle over extra sides and the radio show
summary: Hughes cites Brian Rust listing; she can't explain the separate days and thinks it was around the 'Flow Gently, Sweet Rhythm' radio show.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I should mention that we've been taking most of the discographical material from the Bruyninckx discography. But looking in Brian Rust, we also find listed something which isn't in the Bruyninckx. And that's a session on the 11th of June 1940, also for Columbia, in which two sides were made; 'Mad About The Boy' and 'Under The Greenwood Tree'. And it's with the same personnel as the people who were on the 1st of
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

May 1940 session.
But these sides were never issued. And
I was just wondering if you have any recollection of
them.

I remember the tunes
and I slightly remember having recorded them. I
never knew what happened to them.

Evidently, they didn't release them.
And I also noticed that they were recorded on two
different days -- in fact, more than a month later.

I can't quite understand how we would do
two, and then two later, since we usually did four
selections at the time.

Unless this was due to the switch-over
to Columbia -- the new arrangement -- maybe that's
the only time we had.

I notice the matrix numbers
are not consecutive. So it could be that it was part
of a large John Kirby session in which --

Could be. And it might
be interesting to note, too, that during this time,
we were doing -- we were about to do Flow Gently Sweet
Rhythm Show.
The radio program.
The radio program.
Yeah.
And we might've just switched over and did a couple of dates between shows, or something like that.
We were on every Sunday, and it was a Columbia production. So we were all tied up there together, because these would be things that we would be doing on the show anyway.
So I don't understand how they got separated like that unless --
Unless the others were instrumental.
Um hum. That's about that --
Well that could easily be checked if we look in John Kirby's discography.
Right.
We might find the answer to that.
